sanskrit_verse: कुर्यात् त्रिषवणस्नायी कृच्छ्रं चान्द्रायणं तथा । पवित्राणि जपेत् पिण्डान् गायत्र्याचाभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥
transliteration: kuryāt triṣavaṇasnāyī kṛcchraṃ cāndrāyaṇaṃ tathā | pavitrāṇi japet piṇḍān gāyatryā cābhimantrayet ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who has committed transgression through omission of daily rituals shall perform purification by observing three libations a day, along with Kṛcchra and Cāndrāyaṇa penances; recitation of Pavitra mantras and offering Piṇḍas, while invoking the Gayatri mantra for consecration.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority: Ritual omission disrupts cosmic order and invokes individual dharmic liability.
Causation: Omission leads to spiritual contamination requiring specific remedial action.
Capacity-based responsibility: The offender retains agency to restore balance through prescribed acts.
Restoration logic: Purification restores alignment between individual consciousness and universal dharma.
Consciousness alignment: Invocation of Gayatri reorients awareness toward divine intelligence.

IF contamination level exceeds threshold THEN mandate Pavitra Japa AND Piṇḍa offering sequence.
IF intent deviation present THEN include Abhimantṛya Gayatri activation clause.
IF completion verified THEN remove dharmic liability flag from subject record.
IF non-compliance recurs THEN escalate to higher-capacity supervision framework.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme adjudication, ritual omission is recognized as a breach of ontological duty. Responsibility arises automatically upon commission. Restoration precedes judgment. Penances are not punitive but functional corrections executed under direct supervision of dharma-adhikāris.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes causal link between omission and disorder. Anupūrvaśaḥ governs sequential purification steps. Responsibility aligns proportionally with capacity to act. No infliction occurs—only structured realignment of consciousness through intentional completion.
